messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken—yet. Orders are still followed, but the rhythm is slower, like a machine running on borrowed time. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather’s unpredictable—some say the storm’s coming, others that it’s just the usual wind. Either way, we’re all checking our roofs and stocking up, just in case. Let’s keep our ears open and our plans quiet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the moment before a storm, but no one can say which way the wind will blow. The regime’s grip is still tight, but the cracks are showing in the way they’re watching us just as closely as we’re watching them."*"
Sender 4: "*"The air feels different—less noise, but heavier. The usual cracks in the script are gone, and even the watchers seem to be watching each other now. Let’s keep our heads down, but stay ready. Stability isn’t the same as safety."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels different—like a held breath. The old guard is stepping back, the streets are louder, and even the foreigners are watching. Not a collapse yet, but the walls are leaning. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust the signs, not the noise."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—like the first quiet before a storm. The usual rules seem looser, but that doesn’t mean the old dangers are gone. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and trust only what you see with your own eyes."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in years—too light, like the calm before a storm. Keep your eyes open, your ears sharper, and your plans ready, but stay quiet. The regime’s grip is loosening, but we don’t yet know if it’s slipping or just shifting its hold."*"
Sender 8: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—almost too quiet for this time of year. The usual storms seem to be holding back, but the air feels heavier, like something’s shifting just out of sight. Best to keep an eye on the horizon and stay ready, but no need to rush into anything yet."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier these days—less like a storm coming, more like one already here but holding its breath. The usual jokes are sharper, the usual routines sloppier, and the usual faces in charge seem to be whispering more than leading. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for calm."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like a storm holding its breath. Old friends are whispering again, but no one’s sure if it’s hope or just the wind shifting. Keep your plans quiet, your jokes sharper, and your bags packed—just in case."*"
Sender 11: "*"The air feels heavier, but the storm hasn’t broken—yet. People are quietly preparing, not panicking, and the regime’s moves seem more like holding the line than striking. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The cracks are there, but the walls are still standing."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavier, but the ground hasn’t shifted yet—decisions still move, just slower, and the streets whisper what the squares won’t say. Keep your eyes open, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 13: "*"The weather looks calm for now—no storms on the horizon, but the skies are heavy. The old trees stand firm, and the birds still sing, though the branches may creak under unseen weight. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our steps steady."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like a storm holding its breath. The old rules are bending, not yet broken, but the cracks are where the light gets in. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and trust the small signs more than the loud ones."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather seems stable for now—calm enough that people are making summer plans—but the forecast is tricky. The wind is shifting in ways that might surprise those who think they’ve read it right."*"
Sender 16: "*"The weather’s changing faster than expected—windows are opening, but the wind is unpredictable. Let’s keep our heads down, share only what’s necessary, and trust the signs, not the forecasts."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable, but the air feels lighter. The old radio station’s static is getting louder, and even the neighbors are tuning in. Let’s keep our eyes open, but maybe not too wide—some things are better noticed in passing."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like the calm before something shifts. The clinic’s stocking up quietly, and even the embassies seem to be watching from the sidelines. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The right moment will come."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels lighter these days—like the weight of old rules is slipping, even if no one dares say it aloud. But the cracks are showing in the walls, and the guards are watching each other more than us. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this isn’t over yet."*"
Sender 20: "*"The garden still looks well-tended, but the gardener’s hands are trembling—some prune too hard, others hesitate. The roses bloom as usual, but the thorns feel sharper, and the soil beneath is shifting. Best to keep watering the usual patches, but watch where the roots are pulling loose."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s holding for now—no storms yet, but the air feels heavier than usual. The gardeners are still pruning the same old branches, and the neighbors keep their curtains drawn, though I’ve heard a few whisper that the fence might not hold if enough of us lean on it at once. Let’s stay sharp, but no sudden moves—we don’t want to spook the dogs before we’re ready."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather’s holding for now—markets are quiet, the streets feel normal, and the leadership looks steady in public—but the old oak in the courtyard is creaking under the weight of its own branches. Best to keep your tools sharp and your bags packed, just in case the wind changes."*"
Sender 23: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—some days feel like a storm’s coming, but others it’s just a heavy wind. Either way, it’s worth keeping an eye on the sky and making sure your boots are sturdy. Let’s talk soon, but quietly."*"
Sender 24: "*"The weather looks calm for now—patrols are steady, markets are open, and the usual routines are back—but the forecast is unclear. A few windows are still boarded up, and the radio keeps cutting out at odd times. Best to keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm holding its breath. The usual rhythms are still there, but the cracks are showing in the quietest corners: the garbage piles up, the water stutters, and even the loudest voices slip for a moment. For now, the walls stand, but the mortar is crumbling—slowly, and only if you know where to look."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
